recipes.name: Chicken Taco Filling
ingredients_raw: 1 (1.25 ounce) package dry taco seasoning mix

steps.text: Mix chicken broth and taco seasoning in a bowl.
Place chicken breasts in a slow cooker and pour chicken broth mixture over chicken.
Cover and cook on Low for 6 to 8 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Taco Filling
raw_recipe.description: Slow-cooked chicken breasts need only chicken broth and taco seasoning to make a mean taco filling.

review.reviewBody: I made this in the smaller crockpot yesterday for me. I used homemade taco seasoning and organic chicken broth. It was just what I needed. I portioned out the chicken for my chicken salad lunches for the week, then saved the broth in a seperate freezer container to use for taco soup at a later date. The great thing about this recipe, for me anyway, is that it does double duty!

This just blew me away for how good and how fast and easy it was. I had cooked chicken breasts in the freezer, so instead of cooking this in the slow cooker I simply shredded the chicken, added the taco seasoning (Penzey’s) and broth and cooked it on the stove top until it was heated through and it became somewhat thickened. A couple of tortillas and some typical taco fixins’ and this was a complete meal, a delicious meal, in minutes.

Won't make it this way. Get a 3lb rotisserie chicken from Costco or Smart n final, shred the chicken and put in a pan w the taco seasoning. Use the juice from the rotisserie chicken for moisture, and it won't be soggy. I also will use 16oz sour cream and mix in a package of taco seasoning, to use on the shells.

I made mine in a pressure cooker. Once the steam vented, I cooked for 8 minutes and did he quick release of the pressure. I did add lentil beans as another reviewer did and thought the broth which is now soup was even better than the chicken. We made burritos with the chicken. Delicious.
I made these with fresh corn tortillas. Fried them lightly to a crisp, drained them on a paper towel and made crispy chicken tacos. I added cilantro, lime, guacamole and salsa.

I made this in my Instant Pot pressure cooker. I doubled all the ingredients and cooked it for 15 minutes, then shredded the chicken with a fork. I put the chicken back into the pot with the taco seasoned broth and pushed the saute button to get it to simmer a little bit. Then I scooped the chicken out with a slotted spoon.

I can't really rate this as I didn't really use the recipe. Instead, it gave me the idea how to simplify another recipe I have for my burrito filling. Instead of taco seasoning I used salt, pepper, garlic, cumin and garlic&onion seasoned adobo. I did use half the chicken stock instead of broth and a can of stewed tomatoes, onions, red and green peppers and a can of diced jalopeno peppers and corn. Came out almost as good as my original recipe but much easier.

Like a few other reviewers, I added about a cup of salsa and halved the chicken broth because I love tomatoes. This was delicious. I was tight on time, so I cooked it on high for four hours. The chicken fell apart when I tried to use tongs to transfer it to a board to shred, so I just stirred it with a few forks in the crockpot. I will make this probably once a week going forward and for biannual Mexican fiesta events that I host. Thanks!

I MAKE THIS WITH I PACKAGE TACO SEASONING & 1 SMALL JAR
OF SALSA. IN CROCKPOT FOR 4 HRS. SHRED CHICKEN. USE FOR ALL KINDS O DIDHES. REALLY GOOD 
NO BROTH.

I always rub the seasoning on to the chicken then add salsa over the top and just bake for 35 to 40 min at 375 (check temp)then slice to add to a wrap or taco.....always moist but no soupiness, but in a great sauce !!

I'm recovering from complete knee replacement and wanted to something easy, this was it!! I used six large boneless skinless chicken breast and since I only had one can of chicken broth - I made an additional broth with Sazon Goya ' Con Culantro y Achiote. I also added crushed red pepper and garlic. It came out great. We had tacos the first night, I made a chicken taco salad the next day for lunch and tonight my hubby and I had it again as a chicken taco salad! Will definitely make again.
Since I only had vegetable broth on hand, I added some chicken bouillon granules into it and it worked perfectly.
It wasn't spicy enough for our taste. You could add more spices and use thigh meat to add more flavor and kick it up a notch.

Perfect and easy, tender and delicious! I made a really large batch exactly as written, for a family get together. Everyone loved it. There was a little left today and my nephew went looking for it- and then he asked me how to make it. I will make this again for sure.
3/4/21- loved it!
My family loved this recipe!

We made this recipe as stated and it tasted great! Yes, there was extra liquid in our crock pot but we feel it kept the chicken moist. When eating, we just let the chicken drip a little before building our taco. Next time I make it, I feel that with the juices in my crock pot, I could cook an extra piece or two of chicken and we'd be fine. I know my boys could eat the extra chicken.
Tasty and easy to make. I add chopped green chili’s to add some umph! Served on romaine lettuce leafs.
very good , i added jalepeno for a bit of spice along with crushed red pepper
Very easy and excellent taste. I double the recipe as it is nice to have extra for the week. McCormick Low Sodium Taco works very well and does not add a lot of salt to the tacos.
